To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high frequency ultrasonic signal scattered by a rough surface of clean water and water contaminated by oil substance is a random process.

the scattering of high frequency sound waves from a rough surface is strongly dependent on the physical properties of the scattering surface, and the statistical properties of the backscattered signal are a sensitive indicator of the physical properties of oil substances on the surface.

the statistical properties of the scattered high frequency ultrasonic signal enable the remote, noncontact detection and determination of the principal physical characteristics (density, viscosity and surface tension) of the oil substance layer spread on a rough water surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ultrasonic sensor for remote sensing of the sea surface oil pollution.
the remote sensing of the oil pollution of the water surface using high frequency surface scattering techniques.
the study of the statistical properties of the scattered acoustic signals in the case of high frequency surface waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system is able to detect and identify oil substances on a rough water surface in a contactless and remote way.
the proposed system can be used for remote detection and determination of oil pollution in water bodies.

the proposed remote sensing technique based on the statistical properties of the high frequency surface scattering can be used for the remote sensing and detection of the sea oil spill and for determination of the oil substance properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed system can be used to determine the thickness and viscosity of the oil layer spread on water, the oil density and the oil concentration in the water, as well as the roughness of the water surface.
the remote sensing of the sea surface pollution can be done with the use of the acoustic signal scattered at a high frequency.
the proposed method is a promising tool for remote sensing and detection of the oil pollution on the rough sea surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system can be used to monitor the sea surface oil pollution and to detect the presence of the oil substance on the water surface.
the scattering of high frequency acoustic waves by a layer of oil on a rough water surface is a promising method of remote sensing of the sea surface oil pollution.
the scattering theory can be used to design and build a remote sensing device for detection of the oil pollution on the surface of water.
